explanation: The determinant of a 2x2 matrix is the SIGNED area of the parallelogram built from its two column vectors. The a,c slider set the first column vector and b,d set the second; the shaded region is exactly that parallelogram. When the two columns line up (point the same direction) the parallelogram flattens to zero area, det = 0, and the matrix has no inverse. A negative determinant means the columns are in clockwise (flipped) order.
bullets: det = ad - bc is the signed area spanned by the two column vectors.
det = 0 means the columns are parallel and the matrix is NOT invertible.
The sign of det records orientation: + for counterclockwise, - for flipped.
